problems.title: Problem 1: Colliding block
problems.problem:
A block with a mass $m$ of $10\ \mathrm{kg}$ slides over a smooth surface. Corner D collides with a small fixed block S.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2015-1-fig1.png

Determine the minimum speed $v$ that the block must have so that the block tips over about corner D and lands as shown in the figure. Neglect the size of the small block S. Show clearly how you proceed.
Hint: Assume that during the collision the weight of the block is much smaller than the force of the small block S on the large block.

Hint: Neem aan dat tijdens de botsing het gewicht van het blokje veel kleiner is dan de kracht van het blokje S op het grote blok.

The pulleys rotate without friction and may be regarded as flat homogeneous discs. By timing how long the masses take to move over a certain distance, the acceleration $a$ of the system can be determined. With these data the gravitational acceleration $g$ can be determined.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2015-2-fig1.png

problems.title: Problem 5: Ideal gas
problems.problem:
A system of 1 mol of ideal gas is in a cylinder with a piston. The specific heat at constant volume of the gas is given by $C_V = \tfrac{3}{2}R$. Initially the gas is in equilibrium at a temperature $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ and a pressure $p_1 = 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Two processes are carried out in succession (see figure):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2015-5-fig1.png

Process (1 → 2): The small stop is removed, so that the gas expands irreversibly against a constant external pressure of $p_{ext} = 0.2\cdot 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. The expansion is stopped by means of a second stop when the volume has reached 2 times its original value. The gas then reaches a new equilibrium at temperature $T_2 = T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ and a pressure $p_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}p_1 = 0.5\cdot 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$.
Process (2 → 3): Then the gas is cooled at constant volume to $T_3 = 250\ \mathrm{K}$.
(a) Calculate the heat $Q$ supplied to the system, the work $w$ done on the system, and the energy increase $\Delta U$ of the system. Do the above for each of the 2 processes separately and for the complete process.
(b) Calculate the entropy increase $\Delta S$ of the system for each of the 2 processes separately and for the complete process.

Een systeem van 1 mol ideaal gas bevindt zich in een cilinder met een zuiger. De specifieke warmte bij constant volume van het gas wordt gegeven door $C_V = \tfrac{3}{2}R$. Initieel is het gas in evenwicht bij een temperatuur $T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ en een druk $p_1 = 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. Er worden achtereenvolgens twee processen uitgevoerd (zie figuur):

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2015-5-fig1.png

Proces (1 → 2): Het palletje wordt weggehaald waardoor het gas irreversibel expandeert tegen een constante buitendruk van $p_{ext} = 0{,}2\cdot 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$. De expansie wordt door middel van een tweede palletje gestopt als het volume 2 maal zijn oorspronkelijke waarde heeft bereikt. Het gas vindt hierna een nieuw evenwicht bij temperatuur $T_2 = T_1 = 300\ \mathrm{K}$ en een druk $p_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}p_1 = 0{,}5\cdot 10^5\ \mathrm{Pa}$.
Proces (2 → 3): Daarna wordt het gas bij constant volume afgekoeld naar $T_3 = 250\ \mathrm{K}$.

(b) Bereken de entropie toename $\Delta S$ van het systeem voor elk van de 2 processen apart en voor het complete proces.

problems.title: Problem 12: Lattice model
problems.problem:
A powerful way to illustrate and calculate a number of physical concepts is the so-called lattice model. In it, the space available to a collection of particles is divided into a number of equally large volume units. The volume units are as large as one particle.
(a) Show that the number of ways $\Omega$ to place $N$ identical particles in $M$ volume units ($M \gg N$) is approximately equal to: $\Omega \approx \frac{M^N}{N!}$
(b) Show that the entropy of a system consisting of $N$ identical particles at constant temperature is proportional to the natural logarithm of the volume:
$$s \propto k \ln V$$
Hint: Start by writing down the number of ways in which the particles can be distributed for two different volumes, and calculate the entropy difference between these two situations.
(c) Now consider the mixing process of two different kinds of particles, $A$ and $B$. We take both kinds of particles to be equally large. Initially $N$ identical particles $A$ are in a volume that can be divided into $N_1$ volume units; $M$ identical particles $B$ are initially in $N_2$ volume units. After mixing, all particles $A$ and $B$ are in the combined volume, i.e. in $N_1 + N_2$ volume elements. Calculate the entropy difference between the mixed and the unmixed situation and show that it is always positive.
problems.problem_orig:
Een krachtige manier om een aantal fysische concepten mee te illustreren en door te rekenen is het zogenaamde roostermodel. Hierbij wordt de ruimte die een verzameling deeltjes tot zijn beschikking heeft opgedeeld in een aantal even grote volume-eenheden. De volume-eenheden zijn zo groot als een deeltje.
(a) Laat zien dat het aantal manieren $\Omega$ om $N$ identieke deeltjes in $M$ volume-eenheden ($M \gg N$) te plaatsen, bij benadering gelijk is aan: $\Omega \approx \frac{M^N}{N!}$
(b) Laat zien dat de entropie van een systeem dat bestaat uit $N$ identieke deeltjes bij constante temperatuur evenredig is met de natuurlijke logaritme van het volume:
$$s \propto k \ln V$$
Hint: Begin met het opschrijven van het aantal mogelijkheden waarop de deeltjes verdeeld kunnen zijn voor twee verschillende volumes en bereken het entropieverschil tussen deze twee situaties.
(c) Beschouw nu het mengproces van twee verschillende soorten deeltjes, $A$ en $B$. We nemen beide soorten deeltjes even groot. Aanvankelijk bevinden $N$ identieke deeltjes $A$ zich in een volume dat opgedeeld kan worden in $N_1$ volume-eenheden; $M$ identieke deeltjes $B$ bevinden zich aanvankelijk in $N_2$ volume-eenheden. Na menging bevinden zich alle deeltjes $A$ en $B$ in het gezamenlijke volume, d.w.z. in $N_1 + N_2$ volume-elementen. Bereken het entropieverschil tussen de gemengde en ontmengde situatie en toon aan dat dit altijd positief is.

problems.title: Problem 1: Playing with water

$$t_{grond} = \sqrt{\frac{2L}{g}}\left(\sqrt{\sin^3\alpha + \frac{h}{L}} - \sin^{3/2}\alpha\right)$$

b. Determine the maximum horizontal distance $x$, measured from the lower end of the gutter, that you can reach with the jet of water, and the angle the gutter must then make with the horizontal.

problems.problem:
Consider a cylinder filled with $n = 2.00\ \mathrm{mol}$ of a gas that may be treated as an ideal gas, and of which it is known that the specific heat at constant temperature $c_V$ is equal to $4.000R$. The cylinder is closed by a frictionlessly movable piston with mass $M = 20.00\ \mathrm{kg}$ and area $O = 0.0100\ \mathrm{m^2}$. The cylinder is placed in space as indicated in Figure 1a. The distance between the bottom of the piston and the bottom of the cylinder (the length of the gas column in the cylinder) is $l$. The pressure of the atmosphere is $1.00\ \mathrm{bar}$ and the temperature is $300\ \mathrm{K}$. In this situation there is mechanical and thermal equilibrium: the piston does not change position and the temperature of the gas in the cylinder is equal to that of the surroundings.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2019-4-fig1.png

Figure 1: sketch of the situation for thermodynamic calculations on a cylinder filled with gas. a: vertical arrangement; b: horizontal arrangement. Thermal insulation is indicated by grey bars. The position of the earth is shown by a dark bar.

[Labels in the figure: lucht = air.]

(a) Calculate the pressure of the gas in the given situation corresponding to Figure 1a.
(b) Show that the distance $l$ in the given situation corresponding to Figure 1a is equal to $l = 4.16\ \mathrm{m}$.
The piston is now fixed at the given length of the gas column and the cylinder as a whole is rotated by 90 degrees, as indicated in Figure 1b. At the same time the cylinder is thermally insulated from the surroundings. The piston does not allow any heat exchange with the surroundings either.
Now the piston is no longer held in place, but can move freely again.
(c) Calculate the length and the temperature of the gas column when it is again in equilibrium with the surroundings.
(d) Show that the process of the change in length of the column proceeds spontaneously by calculating the entropy change of the gas and of the surroundings.

problems.title: Problem 6: Bubble-chamber photograph of an electron losing its energy
problems.problem:

A bubble chamber, filled with boiling hydrogen, was widely used to detect collisions of particles with a high energy. As a result of the collisions, electrons are often produced that also have a high energy. Because the electron ionises the hydrogen molecules on its way, it loses energy and, under the influence of the magnetic field present, the electron describes a spiral-shaped path. Each piece of the path can, however, be regarded as part of an ever smaller circle.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2019-6-fig1.png

(a) Derive that the relation between the momentum $p$ of the electron, its charge $q$, the radius $R$ of the path and the magnetic field $B$, which is perpendicular to the plane of the path, is given by $p = BqR$.
It is given that the strength of the magnetic field is $B = 1.2\ \mathrm{T}$.
(b) Show, starting from the relativistic form of the momentum and from the photograph, that the electron has practically the speed of light in a large part of the path.
In the photograph the radius is measured as a function of time. One then finds:
$$R(t) = R(t=0)\,e^{-kt}$$
(c) Calculate the relative decrease of the energy of the electron as a function of time.

problems.title: Problem 12: Shock wave
problems.problem:
In the Second World War renowned physicists and mathematicians such as Taylor, Sedov and Von Neumann worked out a theoretical relation between the propagation speed of a shock wave and the energy of the explosion that causes the shock wave. For a point-like explosion it turns out that, as long as the pressure in the shock wave is greater than the air pressure, the following relation holds for the radius $R$ of the spherical wave as a function of the time $t$:
$$R(t) = kE^{\alpha}\rho^{\beta}t^{\gamma}$$
Here $E$ is the energy released in the explosion and $\rho$ the density of air. The dimensionless constant $k = 1.033$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2020-12-fig1.png
[Visible shock wave in the explosion of an ammunition depot in Russia.]

(a) Determine by dimensional analysis the values of the exponents $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$.
On 13 May 2000 a fireworks storage depot exploded in Enschede. From the roof of a nearby building two firefighters filmed the explosion. On the film the progress of the shock wave can be seen. In March 2001 an article about this appeared in the Nederlands Tijdschrift voor Natuurkunde, containing a graph of the radius of the shock wave as a function of time. The pressure in the shock wave decreases rapidly until it is equal to that of the surrounding air.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2020-12-fig2.png
[The radius of the shock wave as a function of time in the fireworks disaster in Enschede; vertical axis: radius R (m); horizontal axis: time (s).]

(b) Determine as well as possible the moment at which the pressure of the shock wave becomes equal to that of the surrounding air. Indicate how you made the determination.
(c) Using the formula for the radius of the wave as a function of time, make an estimate of the energy released in the explosion. Take for the density of air $\rho = 1.3\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$. Take into account that the shock wave in the fireworks disaster formed a hemisphere.

Voor een puntvormige explosie blijkt, zolang de druk in de schokgolf groter is dan de luchtdruk, de volgende relatie te gelden voor de straal $R$ van de bolvormige golf als functie van de tijd $t$:

Hierin is $E$ de bij de explosie vrijgekomen energie en $\rho$ de luchtdichtheid. De eenheidsloze constante $k = 1{,}033$.

problems.title: Problem 1: Oscillation
problems.problem:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2021-1-fig1.png

(a) Show that the equation of motion is $\ddot{x} = -Cx^3$ and give an expression for $C$. (Hint: for $\alpha \ll 1$: $\sqrt{1+\alpha} = 1 + \frac{\alpha}{2}$)

problems.title: Problem 13: Millikan's experiment
problems.problem:
In Millikan's experiment the elementary charge can be determined in an elegant way.
A very small oil droplet falls downward between two large horizontally mounted capacitor plates. The plates are a distance $h$ apart.
When there is not yet a voltage across the plates, the droplet falls downward with a constant speed $v_1$ between the two dashed lines (a distance $s$ apart). (See the left droplet in the figure.) Three forces then act on the particle: gravity, the buoyant force (in air) and a drag force. For the latter, Stokes' law holds: $F_w = 6\pi\eta r v_1$
Here:
$r$ is the radius of the oil droplet
$\eta$ is the viscosity of air

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2021-13-fig1.png

[Figure labels: $F_z$ = gravitational force; $F_{opw}$ = buoyant force; $F_w$ = drag force; $F_e$ = electric force.]

(a) Show that for the radius of the droplet:
$$r = \sqrt{\frac{9\eta v_1}{2(\rho - d)g}}$$
where:
$\rho$ is the density of the oil
$g$ is the gravitational acceleration
$d$ is the density of air
When the droplet has almost reached the lower plate, a voltage $U_o$ is applied across the plates. As a result the (charged) droplet can move upward again and again has, between the two dashed lines, an (other) constant speed $v_2$. Four forces are now in equilibrium with each other. See also the right droplet in the figure.
(b) Show that:
$$qE = 6\pi\eta r(v_1 + v_2)$$
The speeds $v_1$ and $v_2$ can be found experimentally by successively determining/measuring the time $t_1$ in which the oil droplet falls over a (known) distance $s$ with the electric field switched off, and then the time $t_2$ in which the same droplet rises over the same distance $s$ with the electric field switched on.
(c) Show that for the charge of the droplet:
$$q = \frac{K}{U_0} \cdot \frac{(t_1 \cdot t_2)}{t_1^{3/2} \cdot t_2}$$
In this formula $K$ is a constant that depends on $\eta$, $s$, $h$, $\rho$, $d$ and $g$.
Experimenter Hans carries out measurements on three different droplets. For the apparatus that Hans uses, $K = 3.48 \cdot 10^{-14}\ \mathrm{J\,s^{3/2}}$.
He finds the following values:

$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline \text{Droplet} & \text{Voltage } U_0\ (V) & \text{Time } t_1 (s) & \text{Time } t_2 (s) \\ \hline \#1 & 1130 & 16 & 24 \\ \hline \#2 & 1305 & 27 & 39 \\ \hline \#3 & 850 & 32 & 28 \\ \hline \end{array}$$

(d) Using these measurements, determine the value of the elementary charge. Indicate clearly how you arrived at your answer.

(Zie het linker druppeltje in de figuur.) Er werken dan drie krachten op het deeltje: de zwaartekracht, de opwaartse kracht (in lucht) en een weerstandskracht. Voor deze laatste geldt de wet van Stokes: $F_w = 6\pi\eta r v_1$
Hierin is:
$r$ de straal van de oliedruppel
$\eta$ de viscositeit van lucht

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2021-13-fig1.png

(a) Toon aan dat voor de straal van het druppeltje geldt:
$$r = \sqrt{\frac{9\eta v_1}{2(\rho - d)g}}$$
Met hierbij:
$\rho$ de dichtheid van de olie
$g$ de valversnelling
$d$ de dichtheid van lucht

(a) From the given position of the aircraft, the intensity of the signal from each of the towers is equal to $I_0$. Determine the result the aircraft receives due to the two signals when the aircraft flies in at an angle $\theta = 0$ and also at an angle $\theta = \pi/2$.
(b) At which angles $\theta$ would the aircraft receive no signal? If the aircraft had the instruction to fly in at an angle $\theta = 30^\circ$, what kind of signal would the pilot expect from the two towers?
(c) The aircraft has gone off course and approaches the airport at an angle $\theta = 0^\circ$ and is flying exactly towards one of the towers, i.e. not towards the middle of the runway. The aircraft is still very far away, but the closer it gets, the weaker the signal becomes. How far is the aircraft from the nearest tower when the signal has weakened to the minimum?
problems.problem_orig:
In dit vraagstuk zal een navigatie hulpmiddel voor vliegtuigen die de luchthaven naderen worden onderzocht. Neem aan dat aan het einde van de landingsbaan aan weerszijden een radio zendtoren staat. Deze zendtorens staan op $100\ \mathrm{m}$ van elkaar af. Beide torens zenden een signaal uit met een frequentie $f_0 = 12\ \mathrm{MHz}$ die met elkaar in fase zijn. (b) Onder welke hoeken $\theta$ zou het vliegtuig geen signaal ontvangen? Als het vliegtuig de opdracht had onder hoek $\theta = 30^\circ$ in te vliegen, wat voor soort signaal zou de piloot van de twee torens verwachten?

problems.title: Problem 12: Sound along a fence

What will eventually be the temperature of the ball?

problems.title: Problem 4: Composite system
problems.problem:
Consider a composite system with two subsystems, $L$ and $R$. Both subsystems contain 4 indistinguishable particles. In both subsystems distinguishable energy levels are available, which however differ between the subsystems $L$ and $R$. In subsystem $L$ levels are available with energy 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, etc. In subsystem $R$ the same levels are available with the exception of the level with energy 2. This is shown schematically in the figure below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2023-4-fig1.png

In the initial state the two subsystems are not in thermal or mechanical contact with each other, and together they are and remain thermally insulated from the surroundings. The total energy of subsystem $L$ is 4 and the total energy of subsystem $R$ is 6. Thermal contact is made between the subsystems, which allows the transfer of one or more energy units. Particles cannot be exchanged and the volumes of the subsystems remain the same. A possible process that can take place is the transfer of one energy unit, such that the total energy of both subsystems becomes equal to 5. The process is shown schematically in the figure below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2023-4-fig2.png

(a) Show that the total number of ways $\Omega$ in which 4 indistinguishable particles in subsystem $R$ have a total energy of 6 is equal to 38. Use the attachment.
(b) Show that the entropy of the combined subsystems in the initial state, calculated with the Boltzmann formula, is equal to $S_i = k_B \ln 1330$. Use the attachment.

problems.title: Problem 6: Bungee jumping
problems.problem:
Ad (mass $m = 70\ \mathrm{kg}$) jumps from a platform at a height $h = 90\ \mathrm{m}$ above a lake. A rubber cord with a length $L$ and a spring constant $k$ is attached to Ad's feet (and, fortunately, with the other end to the platform). Neglect Ad's dimensions and the mass of the cord. Neglect air resistance and energy loss, at least until the first time Ad just fails to touch the water.

(a) The rest length $L$ of the cord and the spring constant $k$.
(b) The length of the cord when Ad has finally stopped oscillating and hangs in equilibrium somewhere between the platform and the lake.
(c) The maximum speed $v_{max}$ of Ad.
(d) The time $\tau$ Ad needs to reach the water (almost) for the first time.
For all answers, show clearly how you arrived at your answer. A picture works wonders.

problems.title: Problem 9: A survival manoeuvre

A spaceship, Nostromo, with its engines switched off, orbits a mysterious planet of radius $r$ and mass $P$ in a plane perpendicular to the equatorial plane, following a circular orbit of radius $R=7r$. At the moment the Nostromo is directly above the North Pole, the crew takes a decision: they launch the alien into space, in the direction of motion of the ship. The alien is shot into space with just enough speed to escape the gravitational field of the planet, while the Nostromo itself begins a descent towards the South Pole and approaches the surface of the planet tangentially.

So two scenarios are then possible:

(1) The direction of motion of the ship remains unchanged after the alien is ejected.

(2) The direction of motion of the ship reverses after the alien is ejected.

The speed of the Nostromo (including the alien) just before the alien is ejected is $V_0$, the speed of the Nostromo after the alien is ejected we call $V_N$, and the speed of the alien just after the ejection we call $V_A$.

Answer the following questions:

(a) Derive an expression for $V_0$, expressed in $P$ and $R$.

(b) What is the minimum value of $V_A$ (expressed in $P$ and $R$)?

(c) Derive an expression for $V_N$, expressed in $P$, $R$ and $r$.

(d) Determine, in both cases, the maximum percentage of the total mass of the Nostromo–alien system that the ejected alien can make up. In which of the two scenarios can an alien of larger mass be ejected?

Problem 7: The gunner is amazed

Tony Stark is testing a new training cannon at the Avengers' training base. The cannon fires solid metal balls towards a straight vertical wall. In the first test the ball hits the wall elastically, flies back and lands exactly at the spot from which it was fired. Curious about this strange result, Tony increases the firing angle by $\Delta\alpha$ and fires the cannon again. To his amazement exactly the same thing happens: the ball hits the wall, bounces back and again lands exactly at the starting point. Given the constant initial speed of the ball $v$ and the increase of the firing angle $\Delta\alpha$ between the first and the second shot,

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/physics-olympiads-bank/main/images/nlnno-2026-7-fig1.png

(a) Determine the first firing angle $\alpha_1$.
(b) Determine the distance $L$ between the cannon and the wall.
(c) Determine the smallest possible height $H$ of the wall that makes this situation possible. Neglect air resistance.

problems.title: Problem 9: Pulsars
problems.problem:
Problem 9: Pulsars

Pulsars are a type of rapidly rotating stars of high density, known for their regular pulses of radiation. They are sometimes also called the 'lighthouses of the universe'. In this problem we assume that pulsars are spheres of uniform density that are gravitationally bound.

(a) The rotation period of a pulsar was measured to be $P=1.500\,\mathrm{ms}$. What limit does this place on its density?
(b) If the mass of this pulsar is $1.5M_{\odot}$, what limit can we then place on its radius?

At the end of its lifetime such a star loses about 90% of its mass. The remaining mass (the remnant) forms a pulsar of the type described above. A pulsar is formed from a massive progenitor star which typically has a magnetic field of $0.1\,\mathrm{T}$ and a mean density of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{g\cdot cm^{-3}}$.

(c) Along the lines of part (a), what limit does this place on the rotation period of the progenitor star?
(d) Assuming that the magnetic flux is conserved during the formation of a pulsar, determine the typical magnetic field at the surface of the pulsar?
problems.problem_orig:

In dit vraagstuk nemen we aan dat de pulsars bollen zijn met een uniforme dichtheid, die gravitationeel gebonden zijn.

(a) De rotatieperiode van een pulsar werd gemeten als $P=1{,}500\,\mathrm{ms}$. Welke limiet stelt dit aan de dichtheid ervan?
(b) Als de massa van deze pulsar $1{,}5M_{\odot}$ is, welke limiet kunnen we dan stellen aan de straal ervan?

(c) In de lijn van onderdeel (a), welke limiet stelt dit aan de rotatieperiode van de voorloperster?
(d) Ervan uitgaande dat de magnetische flux behouden blijft tijdens de vorming van een pulsar, bepaal het typische magnetische veld aan het oppervlak van de pulsar?

Problem 11: Hydrogen

When two hydrogen atoms of mass $m$ combine into a diatomic hydrogen molecule ($\mathrm{H_2}$), the potential energy of the system after this combination is equal to $-\Delta$, where $\Delta$ is a positive quantity called the binding energy of the molecule.

(a) Show that in a collision involving only two hydrogen atoms it is impossible to form an $\mathrm{H_2}$ molecule, because momentum and energy cannot be conserved simultaneously.
(b) In a collision between three hydrogen atoms an $\mathrm{H_2}$ molecule can be formed. Suppose that before such a collision each of the three atoms has a speed of $1.00\cdot10^{3}\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and that they approach each other at an angle of $120^\circ$, so that at every moment the atoms form the vertices of an equilateral triangle. Calculate the speeds of the $\mathrm{H_2}$ molecule and of the single hydrogen atom that remains after the collision. The binding energy of $\mathrm{H_2}$ is $\Delta=7.23\cdot10^{-19}\,\mathrm{J}$ and the mass of the hydrogen atom is $1.67\cdot10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}$.
